declared_proposition: For every integer K>=8, put X=K! and H=K-3. The H consecutive lower candidates X+j, 2<=j<=K-2, contain no twin-prime pair, and H >= (1/4) log X/log log X. Consequently there are infinitely many twin-free local windows at least a fixed multiple of the log X/log log X scale. Any proof requiring a twin pair in every window at or below this scale is false.
mathematical_argument: For 2<=j<=K-2, j divides X+j and j+2 divides X+j+2, and both divisors are proper. Thus all H=K-3 lower candidates are twin-free. Also log X<=K log K. The last K/2 factors in K! are at least K/2, so log X>=(K/2)log(K/2), which for K>=8 implies log log X>=(1/2)log K. Hence log X/log log X<=2K, while H=K-3>=K/2, giving H>=(1/4)log X/log log X.
